claims.statement: Both production targets use the shared main-actor ProAccessController, whose live purchase service is RevenueCat configured from the bundled API key and entitlement ID; invalid configuration has no StoreKit fallback and results in verification failure.

The local StoreKit fixture defines a family-shareable lifetime non-consumable and a family-shareable yearly auto-renewable subscription with a two-week free introductory offer, localized for English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.

Only the configured RevenueCat entitlement grants Pro after successful verification; active nonexpiring entitlements map to lifetime access, while subscription access requires an unexpired active trial, subscription or billing-issue grace period and refunds, billing retry and expiration deny access.

RevenueCat customer-info stream updates supersede older controller refreshes, concurrent refreshes share one request, and a failed refresh retains already established access but an initial failure becomes verificationFailed; the service uses a current fetch and falls back to cached CustomerInfo on fetch failure.

The complete entitlement-derived gate vocabulary is assistant, terminal file upload, remote MCP, built-in MCP server, Vault sync and unlimited Metrics; require returns false and raises the shared paywall flag when entitlement is absent, without storing which feature requested it.

Free access retains the ordinary remote-workspace experience and the first three Metrics cards, while protected callers gate assistant execution, terminal drag/drop upload, remote MCP operations, built-in MCP server availability, iCloud synchronization, and Metrics beyond the free limit.

iOS and macOS present RevenueCatUI PaywallView in native sheets, with macOS electing a single main-window owner; both route SDK purchase/restore callbacks into controller processing and status refresh while retaining the account paywall after a successful purchase.

`AppReviewController` records review-request attempts rather than ratings or prompt completion, and only arms an invitation after a qualifying active workspace-to-review-page transition; it requires seven elapsed days, three active dates, five foreground workspace minutes, a per-version budget, and a 120-day cooldown.

App-facing text is defined as semantic `LocalizedStringResource` entries under `Frameworks/TermindPresentation/Strings` and localized in the shared `Frameworks/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings` app catalog; `InfoPlist.xcstrings` owns bundle metadata. New or changed English app text needs finished `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` translations; the default Chinese check validates both app catalogs' normalization, JSON, Chinese completion and spacing, not AgentKit or website copy.

The iOS widget extension contains only a workspace Live Activity; its payload excludes credentials and terminal output, is bounded to six focused-first summaries, and its strict deep links route to the workspace list or a UUID-addressed workspace.

`ScreenshotDemoConfiguration` is DEBUG-only and binds one validated demo scene to one of English, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese; the screenshot helper builds TFM and launches it with matching application language and locale overrides.

The Astro marketing site is a separate `LandingPage` app whose build runs `astro check && astro build`, and it imports an explicit allowlist of framed assets rather than serving copied sources from the public directory.

For a granting subscription with a future known deadline the controller cancels its previous expiration timer and schedules a refresh at that deadline, while both app targets also refresh access on activation; the timer does not directly revoke access.

Live RevenueCat access is used outside tests and in-memory/demo setups; status changes reconcile macOS sync and built-in MCP, whereas iOS reconciles sync on access and scene changes and requires an active foreground scene.

Current AppLanguageTests checks language preference migration, Chinese regional lookup, token terminology, forwarding placeholders and selected plurals but no longer tests explicit-language Pro offers; whole-catalog Chinese completion is enforced by the shell checker rather than these tests.

StoreKitTrialTests is opt-in with TERMIND_STOREKIT_TESTS=1 and uses SKTestSession only to validate local lifetime/annual product shape and annual free introductory metadata, not RevenueCat purchase, restore or access transitions.

On iOS, Vault and Vault search open Snippets and Known Hosts with optional initial queries; Known Hosts distinguishes empty library from empty search results, offers add from the toolbar and edit/copy-fingerprint/delete per card, and selects add versus edit editor title based on whether the entry already exists.

On macOS, the Known Hosts empty state offers import or manual add; deletion has singular/plural localized confirmation text and warns that deleting trust means verifying the server key on the next connection, while editor labels distinguish adding and editing.

Mobile Snippets distinguishes an empty library from no search matches, offers new snippets, packages and nested subpackages, and gives package deletion a remove-with-snippets or keep-snippets choice; its package-deletion message selects a count-sensitive shared resource, while section-header counts are locale-formatted numbers.

Known-host and snippet card relative timestamps use the SwiftUI environment locale, while host titles, package paths, snippet titles, and script bodies are record content displayed directly instead of localized catalog keys.

Current AppLanguageTests covers Chinese lookup, assistant/security-token terminology, forwarding placeholders and selected plurals but not Pro offer formatting; mobile card tests cover editor titles and optional real-window multilingual captures, while the catalog checker covers whole-catalog Chinese completion.

AppStrings groups semantic LocalizedStringResource definitions in TermindPresentation/Strings for TFM and TFI, including single-platform text; platform-specific wording uses explicit variants and protocol values, identifiers and diagnostic codes stay with their existing owners.

App-facing resource text is resolved at presentation time from the main app bundle using the requested locale, while the SwiftUI key bridge preserves resource metadata and shared formatting composes localized counts/messages without translating user-authored values or caching language-specific strings.

The SwiftSyntax AppStrings checker scans TFM and TFI for selected UI literals and verifies the shared Strings/AppStrings owner file exists, while ArchitectureBoundaryTests guards the AppStrings owner and dependencies; these static checks complement the Chinese catalog check and runtime localization tests rather than proving all copy is reusable or properly rendered.

Both shared app string catalogs are manually managed: normalization sets every extraction state to manual and canonical Xcode formatting without deleting stale keys or altering translations, while the Chinese check verifies normalized catalogs and completed Simplified and Traditional units; stale extraction from one target is not grounds to delete a shared key.

`AppLanguage` writes canonical explicit-language tags to `AppleLanguages`, removes the override for Follow System, migrates older Simplified Chinese preferences and treats unsupported stored tags as system language; catalog lookup selects the effective app-bundle localization including regional Traditional Chinese.
Pro-dependent sync reconciliation starts or pauses Vault, connection-history, device, Metrics, and Settings coordinators on both platforms; mobile additionally requires an active foreground scene.

The mobile Metrics host picker passes current entitlement to a three-card free cap through MobileMetricsModel.replaceHosts; a failed replacement shows the core storage error if present, otherwise presents the Pro paywall.

When a SwiftUI API accepts `LocalizedStringResource` directly, particularly `confirmationDialog`, passing the resource rather than its `swiftUIKey` avoids exposing interpolated locale metadata through UIKit-backed presentation; `swiftUIKey` is reserved for APIs requiring `LocalizedStringKey`.

The shared Metrics model preserves selections outside the edited host picker, admits only net additions within the current card limit, and persists a selected-host replacement in a single operation; desktop supplies a live entitlement-based limit and invokes `require(.unlimitedMetrics)` on rejection.

The public Astro site's FAQ owns the website's free/Pro feature descriptions, Family Sharing, device-specific MCP and AI provider billing disclosures independently of native catalogs; site copy selects English, Simplified Chinese or converted Taiwan Traditional through `LandingPage/src/lib/i18n.ts`.

The landing site's allowlisted framed marketing images come directly from Marketing/Screenshots/DeviceFrames; production Astro builds transform imported sources into AVIF, WebP, and JPEG outputs rather than copying source screenshots or frames into LandingPage/public.

The catalog normalizer defaults to the two shared app catalogs, marks entries manual without deleting stale translations, rejects duplicate JSON keys before any batch write, and checks or writes Xcode-compatible serialization; AgentKit's separately owned runtime catalog requires its own localization build step.

The public security and privacy pages are separate Astro components routed through locale page wrappers and BaseLayout, which provides locale-aware navigation and canonical/alternate links and stores the selected website language in browser localStorage independently of native app language preferences.

The public privacy page discloses local and iCloud/Keychain data, Apple purchase handling alongside RevenueCat validation, entitlement sync, anonymous ID association and paywall service, optional network/AI processing and diagnostics, deletion controls and website-local language preference with possible hosting logs.

The public security page describes Keychain-backed software credentials and one-shot secret-buffer cleanup, Known Hosts checks, configurable Assistant permissions, and the opt-in Mac-only loopback MCP server's local bearer token and exposed-tool controls, warning that authenticated clients need not confirm every tool call; this marketing copy is a disclosure to compare with runtime behavior, not independent proof of an end-to-end security guarantee.

The landing-page homepage embeds a separate Telegram draw offer for a chance to win a Pro redemption code on Thursdays, linking to a channel, group, and entry bot; the copy explicitly disclaims guaranteed wins and defers redemption eligibility and validity to Apple, rather than representing a StoreKit plan or a guaranteed free trial.

RevenueCatProPurchaseService uses anonymous app user IDs rather than a device or iCloud account ID, configures StoreKit 2 with informational entitlement verification and disabled automatic device identifier collection, and supplies the stored language as preferred RevenueCat UI locale.

For a non-test-store user without Pro, RevenueCatProPurchaseService attempts to import pre-integration purchases via syncPurchases at most once per successful anonymous user ID migration and skips migration on verification failure.

Both native paywalls send ProPaywallState protocol variables for access, subscription management, family ownership, status and localized expiration to the remote dashboard; only purchaser-owned subscriptions expose the management variable and missing dates are not invented.

RevenueCatCommerceTests exercises configured entitlement resolution, grace deadlines, refund and verification failures, remote paywall completion, streamed updates, concurrent and racing refreshes, unavailable service and fetch failure recovery, rather than testing the remote paywall design or real purchases.

Current native paywall surfaces display a localized loading state and an unavailable fallback without a RevenueCat service, but leave the offer layout, trial terms and legal links to RevenueCatUI rather than constructing them from local paywall presentation types.

The local StoreKit fixture is metadata-only for commerce testing, not a guarantee of production RevenueCat paywall availability, purchase or trial eligibility; the manually opted-in test validates product type, Family Sharing, yearly term and two-week free introductory offer.
